blocks.content: The area bounded by the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn receives the maximum heat and is called the Torrid Zone.

items: Examiners frequently test exact latitude values: Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N), Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S), Arctic Circle (66.5° N), and Antarctic Circle (66.5° S).
The mid-day sun is exactly overhead at least once a year on all latitudes in the Torrid Zone only.
Angle of the sun rays decreases continuously towards the poles, causing temperatures to decrease from the Equator towards the Polar region.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Earth is divided into three main heat zones based on the amount of direct sunlight received: Torrid, Temperate, and Frigid.
The Torrid Zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5° S) and receives maximum heat.
The Temperate Zones lie between 23.5° and 66.5° in both hemispheres, featuring moderate climate and slanting sun rays.
The Frigid Zones are located beyond 66.5° N and S up to the poles, experiencing extreme cold because the sun never rises high above the horizon.
